Listen to this article Share Nigeria needs stronger collaboration between government institutions, regulators, businesses and cybersecurity professionals to tackle growing digital threats, according to Eric Schifflers, Group Chief Information Security Officer and Head of Governance, Risk and Compliance at TeKnowledge. Advertisement Advertisement Speaking at a conference hosted by the International Information System Security Certification Consortium (ISC2) Nigeria Chapter, Schifflers said the country’s next cybersecurity challenge was to move beyond regulatory compliance towards a more coordinated approach that enables organisations to prevent, respond to and recover from cyberattacks. Addressing participants on the theme, From Compliance to Collaboration: Building Nigeria’s Cyber Defence Ecosystem, he noted that cybersecurity had evolved beyond an IT concern to become an issue of economic stability, institutional resilience and national security. He highlighted the growing sophistication of cyber threats, including attacks targeting critical infrastructure and digital supply chains, as well as AI-enabled fraud, misinformation, privacy breaches and other forms of digital deception. According to him, the interconnected nature of modern business operations means that a security breach affecting one organisation can have wider consequences for other businesses, government institutions and citizens. Schifflers acknowledged Nigeria’s progress in establishing a regulatory and institutional framework for cybersecurity, citing the Cybercrimes Act, the National Cybersecurity Policy and Strategy, the Nigeria Data Protection Act and national response capabilities such as the Nigerian Computer Emergency Response Team (ngCERT). Advertisement However, he cautioned that having regulations in place does not necessarily guarantee that organisations or industries can withstand cyber incidents. “A compliant organisation can still be breached. A well-regulated industry can still suffer systemic disruption,” he said. Advertisement He argued that cybersecurity efforts should therefore extend beyond individual organisations meeting regulatory requirements to building stronger relationships between institutions that share digital infrastructure and operational dependencies. Financial institutions, for instance, rely on telecommunications networks, data centres and payment infrastructure, while government agencies increasingly depend on cloud services, identity platforms and third-party applications. These interconnected systems, he explained, create opportunities for attackers to exploit vulnerabilities in one organisation to gain access to others. Advertisement Advertisement Schifflers said addressing these risks would require greater cooperation between regulators, government agencies, critical infrastructure operators, technology companies and cybersecurity professionals. He also identified trust as a critical component of effective cyber defence, particularly when it comes to sharing threat intelligence and coordinating responses to security incidents. Among the questions organisations should be considering, he said, was whether they could exchange threat intelligence quickly enough to contain an attack, whether regulators and industry operators could work together during an incident, and whether competing businesses could collaborate on threats affecting the wider digital ecosystem. The increasing adoption of artificial intelligence also featured in his presentation, with Schifflers highlighting the importance of data governance as organisations integrate AI tools into their operations. He said businesses needed to establish clear controls around data ownership, classification, storage and access, as well as determine what information employees could share with AI applications and how such interactions would be monitored. He stressed that cybersecurity and governance should support, rather than hinder, technological innovation, particularly as Nigerian businesses accelerate their digital transformation efforts. Schifflers called for more public-private cybersecurity exercises, stronger intelligence-sharing arrangements across industries, closer coordination with critical infrastructure operators and increased collaboration between industry and academic institutions. He emphasised that these relationships needed to be established before a cyber incident occurred, rather than during an emergency when organisations would already be under pressure to contain the damage. “When an attack is underway, organisations should not be exchanging introductions; they should already know who to call, what information can be shared and how coordinated decisions will be made,” he said. He added that the ultimate objective should be to build an ecosystem capable of anticipating threats, managing disruption and recovering quickly, rather than focusing solely on preventing cyberattacks. As Nigeria continues to expand its digital economy, strengthening cooperation across its cybersecurity ecosystem will be increasingly important to protecting businesses, public institutions and citizens from evolving digital threats. Ifeoma Okeke-Korieocha Ifeoma Okeke-Korieocha is the Aviation Correspondent at BusinessDay Media Limited, publishers of BusinessDay Newspapers. She is also the Deputy Editor, BusinessDay Weekender Magazine, the Saturday Weekend edition of BusinessDay. She holds a BSC in Mass Communication from the prestigious University of Nigeria, Nsukka and a Masters degree in Marketing at the University of Lagos. As the lead writer on the aviation desk, Ifeoma is responsible and in charge of the three weekly aviation and travel pages in BusinessDay and BDSunday. She also overseas and edits all pages of BusinessDay Saturday Weekender. She has written various investigative, features and news stories in aviation and business related issues and has been severally nominated for award in the category of Aviation Writer of the Year by the Nigeria Media Nite-Out awards; one of the Nigeria’s most prestigious media awards ceremonies. Ifeoma is a one-time winner of the prestigious Nigeria Media Merit Award under the 'Aviation Writer of the Year' Category. She is the 2025 Eloy Award winner under the Print Media Journalist category. She has undergone several journalism trainings by various prestigious organisations. Ifeoma is also a fellow of the Female Reporters Leadership Fellowship of the Wole Soyinka Centre for Investigative Journalism.
